page: Vultr vc2-2c-2gb is an entry-level virtual machine within the Vultr Cloud Compute product line. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, offering two virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are provisioned on a shared allocation basis. The CPU architecture incorporates hardware capabilities including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA instructions, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and a 16 MB L3 cache pool.

System memory consists of 2.0 GB of RAM, allocating 1.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 65 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPU accelerators provisioned on this instance. Memory bandwidth benchmarks yield 177.44 GB/s for small cached reads, dropping to 12.18 GB/s for large uncached block reads and 10.85 GB/s for writes.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate entry-tier performance across synthetic suites. Stress-ng scores show 1260.88 for single-core execution and 2444.49 for multi-core, both ranking in the lower quartile of tracked hardware. In the PassMark benchmark suite, the instance registers an overall CPU score of 2453.98 and a memory score of 938.79. Application-level metrics record 1.39 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 1.72 GB/s. Small model LLM inference reaches 115.73 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 32.64 tokens/sec for generation on a 135M parameter model.

The shared CPU allocation and limited 2 GB memory footprint represent clear tradeoffs against sustained compute stability and large in-memory footprints. However, the bundled NVMe storage provides rapid local disk access at an entry-level infrastructure tier. Vultr vc2-2c-2gb is best aligned with lightweight utility workloads, including small-scale web serving, microservices, lightweight development environments, DNS hosting, and non-critical edge automation.
